描述_EN: baas first produced plastic chair in wood in 2008 whilst participating in contrast gallery’s residency program which brought western artists to china to study local artistic and cultural practices. baas’ plastic chair in wood is the antithesis to the anonymous mass manufactured one piece monobloc (also in the collection w.35-2016) which was designed to be affordable by all parts of society. baas’ chair design challenges the idea of value and is full of the contradictions he found inherent in china (especially shanghai) ranging from the cheap looking to the luxuriously expensive, high tech versus low tech, notions of originality versus the disposable copy, and the mass produced item versus the one-off hand-crafted. each chair in this edition is hand carved from pieces of elm wood in shanghai by a group of craftsmen of various different skill types which include a type of chinese joinery of slotting wood together with glue. it was included in the inaugural exhibition, ‘values of design’, in the v&a gallery at design society in a section exploring the critical issue of cost as a value in design. maarten baas’ pieces, although produced in a series, are all uniquely handmade. baas became interested in woodworking and challenged woodcarvers from shanghai to make works which were a hybrid between western design practice and traditional chinese craft techniques. he has produced a chair which seems to embody all these contradictions as well as challenging the viewer to simply consider the aesthetic design of the humble plastic monobloc when the material and production processes are removed from the intrinsic necessity of its production. the labour and natural wood grain found in the elm gives each chair a distinctive character over the anonymous aesthetic of the monobloc. the chair was assigned an edition number of 34 from a series of 50. this chair was acquired as part of the shekou project, an international partnership between the v&a and china merchant shekou holdings (cmsk) to open a new cultural platform called design society in shekou. this is due to the painstaking hand-made recreation of the form itself, utilising a human labour force of specialised skills, and multi-piece construction utilising glue and joinery as opposed to the instantaneous process of plastic injection moulding which allowed a one piece chair to be developed. the final result is then varnished.
描述_ZN: 2008年，Baas在参加对比画廊的驻场项目时首次制作了木质塑料椅，该项目将西方艺术家带到中国，研究当地的艺术和文化实践。 巴斯的木质塑料椅与匿名的大规模制造的单体椅（也在w.35-2016系列中）相对立，后者的设计是为了让社会各阶层都能负担得起。 巴斯的椅子设计挑战了价值的概念，充满了他在中国（尤其是上海）发现的固有矛盾，从廉价的外观到奢华的价格，高科技与低科技，原创的概念与一次性的复制，以及大规模生产的物品与一次性的手工制作的矛盾。 本版中的每把椅子都是由一群具有不同技能的工匠在上海用榆木片手工雕刻而成，其中包括一种用胶水将木头缝合在一起的中国榫卯工艺。 该作品被列入设计协会画廊的首届展览 "设计的价值 "中，在探索成本作为设计价值的关键问题的部分。 马腾-巴斯的作品，虽然是系列化生产，但都是独特的手工制作。 年¥Baas开始对木工感兴趣，并挑战来自上海的木匠，使作品成为西方设计实践和中国传统工艺技术之间的混合体。 他制作了一把椅子，似乎体现了所有这些矛盾，同时也挑战了观众，当材料和生产过程被从其生产的内在必要性中移除时，他们会简单地考虑简陋的塑料单体的美学设计。 在榆木中发现的劳动和自然木纹使每把椅子都具有独特的特征，而不是单体的匿名美学。 这把椅子被分配了一个版本号，从50个系列中的34个。 这把椅子是作为Shekou项目的一部分被收购的，这是V&A和中国商人Shekings（Cmsk）之间的一个国际合作项目，目的是在Shekou开设一个新的文化平台，称为设计社会。 这是由于对形式本身的艰苦手工制作，利用人类劳动力的专业技能，以及利用胶水和细木工的多件结构，而不是允许开发一体式椅子的塑料注射成型的即时过程。 最后的结果是清漆。
